title: Span Pivot Panel and Correlation Quickfilters
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Operators and engineers exploring slow or noisy requests currently jump between the timeline, raw span list, and full trace view. This disconnect makes it hard to answer questions like 'which downstream spans correlate with high token cost' or 'are these tail-latency requests dominated by a single span type?'

Goal: Design a compact, persistent panel that lets users 'pivot' the current request view by a span attribute (service, op name, resource, span tag) while surfacing one-click correlation quickfilters (correlation IDs, request attributes, runtime tags). The feature should speed up triage by reducing context switches and by making high-signal spans and correlated requests visible within two clicks.

Scope: Console tracing workspace only (not the historical exports). Prototype for desktop web; mobile adjustments are out of scope for this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Pivot panel anchored to right side of request detail when enabled
Selecting a pivot attribute highlights matching spans in timeline and collapses other spans to a summary row
Quickfilters surface top 5 correlated attributes (by frequency and latency contribution) and can be applied without leaving the current trace
Prototype includes keyboard shortcuts: 'p' to open pivot, '/' to focus quickfilters
Design tokens for collapsed summary rows, highlight color, and badge counts documented in Figma and ready for handoff
decisions: Keep pivot panel horizontally adjacent to timeline (right rail) instead of replacing timeline to preserve temporal context
Aggregate non-selected spans into a single collapsed row rather than progressive hiding to maintain absolute time position
Quickfilters will be computed server-side as a pre-aggregated top-K per trace window for performance; UI will fetch a small summary endpoint
Initial pivot attributes: service, op_name, resource, span.kind, tag:user_id (expandable later)
tradeoffs: Pros: Enables fast triage without losing timeline context. Cons: Additional right-rail real estate reduces space for long timeline; mitigated by collapsible panel and responsive layout
Server-side pre-aggregation reduces client CPU but requires a new trace-summary API and a caching TTL decision (default 30s)
Highlighting many spans can stress rendering; we chose aggregated summary rows and virtualization to limit DOM updates
tasks: Finalize Figma variant with 3 data density states (compact, normal, expanded)
Create ENG ticket for UI work: ENG-223977 (Pivot panel shell + keyboard shortcuts)
Create ENG ticket for backend summary endpoint: ENG-223978 (trace-summary pre-aggregations)
Plan 5-session usability study with infra on-call and 3 customer-rep accounts
Add accessibility review pass (contrast and keyboard flow)
Write acceptance test checklist and demo script for release review
reviews: 2025-02-12: PM review (Jonas Miller) - asked to include 'cost-per-request' badge in pivot row; accepted as optional early experiment
2025-02-13: Eng sync (Ravi Patel) - raised rendering perf risk for traces >5k spans; agreed engineering will add virtualization and cap high-density highlights behind a toggle
2025-02-14: Security (Aisha Khan) - confirmed no new PII surface introduced; quickfilters will respect existing RBAC and log redaction policies
2025-02-15: Accessibility review (Nora Voss) - requested focus order improvements for quickfilters and explicit aria-live region when pivot updates applied
notes: Usability note: users expect pivot context to persist when switching between similar traces; consider a lightweight URL state (query param) for bookmarks
Performance note: for traces with streaming spans, we should debounce pivot recalculation to 300ms to avoid thrashing the UI
Follow-up experiment: surface an estimated 'token cost delta' next to pivot rows (requires signals from runtime-cost pipeline)
Handoff checklist to ENG: include Figma tokens, CSS variable map, keyboard interactions, and a small dataset json (sample traces with 20-200 spans) for storybook stories
